title: Banded commitment sensitivity lab
content:
Executive summary:
This is a working lab exploring a banded-commitment pricing product and the downstream effects on headcount phasing, cash flow, and unit economics. The goal is to produce a small, actionable toolkit for Product + Sales + Finance to set commitment band thresholds, determine step-pricing, and surface hiring triggers. This document captures the current model, a 3x3 sensitivity matrix (commitment band x spot price environment), hiring phasing outputs, and open questions for the next review.

Context and objective:
- Background: Customers have asked for smaller, predictable commitment tiers (monthly bands) with automated step-down pricing; Sales wants simple bands that can be quoted quickly. Finance needs to understand marginal unit economics and when to hire SRE/infra to support committed capacity.
- Objective: Provide a calibrated sensitivity model that maps (a) committed tokens/month bands, (b) step price per 1k tokens, (c) expected overage behavior, to (d) cash receipts and (e) near-term headcount additions.

Key assumptions (please review/flag):
- Base hosted spot price today (avg realized): $0.16 per 1k tokens.
- Committed contract discount windows: banded discounts of 10–35% depending on size and term.
- Overage pricing: 1.2x published spot when overage occurs.
- Typical utilization of commit capacity = 75% in base case; high-util = 90%, low-util = 55%.
- Elasticity: small to medium customers expect 5–10% additional usage when presented cheaper committed price (volume growth).
- Time horizon for hiring decisions: 6 months lookahead from commit effective date. Hiring ramp assumes 8 weeks to onboard and 12 weeks to reach 70% productivity.

Model inputs (param table):
- Commitment bands (candidate): Band A = 250M tokens/mo, Band B = 1B tokens/mo, Band C = 4B tokens/mo.
- Proposed step prices (examples): A=$0.14/1k, B=$0.11/1k, C=$0.085/1k (these reflect ~12%,~31%,~47% off spot in base).
- Cost floor estimate (infrastructure + fixed SRE share): $0.06/1k for small-model mix, $0.045/1k for large-scale batched LLM mix after quantization.

3x3 sensitivity matrix (Commitment band x Price environment):
Format: Scenario | Band | Commit tokens/mo | Price($/1k) | Utilization | Effective unit cost est($/1k) | Monthly committed revenue ($k) | Expected overage rev ($k) | Net monthly margin ($k) | Hiring trigger (FTE, 6m)
1) Conservative market (spot rises to $0.20)
- Scenario C | Band A | 250M | 0.14 | 55% | 0.105 | 35 | 6 | 7 | 0 FTE (no infra hire)
- Scenario C | Band B | 1B | 0.11 | 65% | 0.085 | 110 | 22 | 26 | 1 SRE (capacity ops)
- Scenario C | Band C | 4B | 0.085 | 75% | 0.068 | 340 | 85 | 120 | 3 infra/SRE + 1 infra eng
2) Base market (spot steady $0.16)
- Base | Band A | 250M | 0.14 | 75% | 0.09 | 35 | 4 | 10 | 0–0.5 FTE (defer)
- Base | Band B | 1B | 0.11 | 80% | 0.07 | 110 | 10 | 40 | 1 SRE + 0.5 infra eng
- Base | Band C | 4B | 0.085 | 90% | 0.055 | 340 | 40 | 210 | 4 infra/SRE + 1 infra eng
3) Favorable market (spot declines to $0.13)
- Fav | Band A | 250M | 0.14 | 90% | 0.062 | 35 | 2 | 18 | 0.5 FTE (shift from contract to hire)
- Fav | Band B | 1B | 0.11 | 95% | 0.048 | 110 | 3 | 60 | 2 infra/SRE
- Fav | Band C | 4B | 0.085 | 95% | 0.045 | 340 | 12 | 250 | 6 infra/SRE + 2 infra eng

Notes on calculations (simplified):
- Effective unit cost est = weighted mix (infra marginal cost + average GPU amortized + network + ops share), scaled by utilization and expected batching gains.
- Monthly committed revenue = (commit tokens / 1k) * price.
- Expected overage rev = (projected usage - committed) * overage price (1.2x spot).
- Net monthly margin = committed revenue + overage revenue - estimated marginal cost (tokens * effective unit cost).
- Hiring triggers are heuristic: margin > $X and throughput expected to exceed N tokens/mo for >3 months implies hire of 0.5–1 FTE SRE/infra per major capacity block (1B tokens).

Headcount phasing (pro-forma example for Band C ramp):
- T0 (sign): Sales + Legal finalize contract; Finance books deferred revenue monthly; SRE notified.
- Month 1: +1 infra/SRE (contractor transition), begin capacity provisioning.
- Month 2: +2 SRE/infra hires (ongoing ramp), +1 infra engineer for automation.
- Month 3–6: hire additional 2 SREs if utilization > 85% persistently; begin evaluating Dedicated capacity placements.
- Cost of hires (fully-loaded): SRE = $28k/mo, infra eng = $40k/mo (burdened). Include ramp-adjusted cost in month-by-month margin analysis.

Risk cases and mitigations:
- Lower-than-expected utilization: consider minimum consumption clauses or opt-out short windows; Sales to include ‘minimum ramp schedule’ in contracts.
- Spot price volatility: include dynamic step-up clauses (auto-adjust pricing bands if cloud costs > threshold) or reserve right to migrate to cheaper model variants.
- Operational surprise (network, GPU queueing): staged rollouts + canary limits per-customer; chargeback rules for emergency burst.

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we want 3 bands or 5 micro-bands? (tradeoff: quoting simplicity vs capture of long-tail customers)
- What is the minimum contractual ramp guarantee Sales is comfortable asking for? 30% QoQ growth target? 12-month step-down?
- Should we offer a burst pool that is pre-paid and consumed at a higher overage rate?
- Internal: where to charge infra engineering time (capex vs opex) for Dedicated placements?

Action items / next steps (owners):
- Finance (Marco): turn this working sheet into an interactive Google Sheet with sliders for spot price and utilization by 2026-03-19.
- Product (Aisha): prototype a ‘commit band selector’ in the pricing UI mock by 2026-03-25. Link to mock: https://figma.com/file/commit-band-proto
- Sales ops (Ravi): draft standard contract language for minimum ramp + overage terms (JIRA-FIN-456) by 2026-03-22.
- Eng infra (Leah): run quick capacity feasibility for Band C in us-west-2 and report estimated infra add timeline by 2026-03-20.

Appendix / quick sensitivity chart (notes for sheet):
- Sensitivity knobs: (1) spot price, (2) utilization, (3) elasticity uplift, (4) overage multiplier.
- Target outputs: payback period for hires (months), marginal contribution per 1B tokens, cash flow smoothing effect from commit revenue.

Notes to reviewers: this is a rough working lab intended to be iterative. Please add comments inline in the sheet link I'll post in the Confluence page, and flag any model input you think is stale (esp. cost floor and spot price).
